newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan finance groups launch investment firms.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan finance groups launch investment firms.

text.p: Moroccan banks and financial institutions on Monday launched two new companies to attract public savings for investment in shares on the Casablanca stock exchange and state-backed bonds.

The companies, Inmaa Croissance and Inmaa Patrimoine, will have initial capital respectively of 15 million dirhams ($1.7 million) and 10 million dirhams ($1.1 million) and are to be listed on the Casablanca stock exchange.

Shares with a face value of 1,000 dirhams were being offered for sale from Monday, said an official with one of the promoting companies, the Banque Nationale pour le Developpement Economique (BNDE). Non-residents can also subscribe to shares.
"With Inmaa Croissance 60 percent of investment will go into shares listed on the Casablanca bourse, while 40 percent will go into bonds," the official said.
"For Inmaa Patrimoine it will be the reverse -- 60 percent into bonds issued and guaranteed by the state."
Besides the BNDE, 10 other financial institutions are promoting Inmaa Croissance, while the BNDE and six other firms are behind Inmaa Patrimoine.
